sentences.text: You will not be moved.
Lord, as sleep comes, I place myself completely in your hands.
My body, my mind, my heart, my family, my tomorrow.
Watch over me through the night, and wake me to your mercy in the morning.
And now receive this blessing as you sleep.
Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means.
The Lord be with you all.
Sleep well, in the shelter of his love.
In Jesus' name, amen.

rubric.reasons: Opens with an affirming declaration, flows into a complete bedtime surrender, and closes with a gentle priestly blessing.
rubric.hook_line: You will not be moved tonight
rubric.title: A Bedtime Blessing for Deep Peace

shortlist.hook: You will not be moved tonight
shortlist.title: A Bedtime Blessing for Deep Peace

sentences.text: You can lean your whole weight on him, and he will not move.
I have set the LORD always before me:
because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth:
my flesh also shall rest in hope.
Thou wilt shew me the path of life:
in thy presence is fulness of joy;
at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
My flesh also shall rest in hope.
Your body can rest tonight, not because every problem is solved, but because your hope is in God.
He is at your right hand.
You will not be moved.

rubric.reasons: Powerful first line, complete biblical exposition, and loops back into its opening theme seamlessly.
rubric.hook_line: Lean your whole weight on Him
rubric.title: You Can Lean Your Whole Weight

sentences.text: Father, I also bring you what I regret.
The impatient word.
The thing I should have done and did not.
The moment I chose myself over someone else.
I do not want to carry guilt into my sleep.
I confess it to you honestly, and I receive your forgiveness.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Faithful and just.
God does not forgive you reluctantly.
He forgives you because he promised he would, and he always keeps his promises.
So tonight you can lay your head down clean.

rubric.reasons: Tackles nighttime regret honestly and delivers immense emotional release with the closing promise of laying down clean.
rubric.hook_line: Don't carry guilt into your sleep
rubric.title: Lay Your Head Down Clean Tonight

sentences.text: To you the night may feel long and heavy.
To God, it shines like the day.
He sees you as clearly at midnight as he did at noon.
Nothing that happens in the dark is hidden from him, and nothing in the dark can separate you from his love.
Lord, I give you my thoughts.
When my mind starts replaying the day or rehearsing tomorrow, bring it back to you.
Replace every anxious thought with a promise from your word.
Let my last thoughts tonight be thoughts of your goodness.
Jesus said, Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you:
not as the world giveth, give I unto you.
Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

rubric.reasons: Outstanding opening contrast between human darkness and God's light, carrying strong emotional reassurance throughout.
rubric.hook_line: Midnight is not dark to God
rubric.title: When the Night Feels Too Heavy

sentences.text: One by one, I open my hands and give them to you.
I cannot solve them tonight.
You can hold them while I sleep.
Jesus said, Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me;
for I am meek and lowly in heart:
and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Jesus promises rest for your souls.
Sleep can rest your body, but only he can rest the part of you that keeps running even when your eyes are closed.

sentences.text: Casting all your care upon him;
for he careth for you.
To cast something is to throw it, to let it leave your hands.
Not to set it down beside the bed so you can pick it up again at three in the morning.
And the reason is the most tender line in the verse:
for he careth for you.
God is not tired of your worries.
He wants them.
Father, I name my worries before you now.
The one about money.
The one about my health.
The one about someone I love.
The conversation that went badly.
The thing I am afraid will happen tomorrow.

rubric.reasons: Brilliant insight about casting versus picking worries back up at 3 AM, but ends unresolved while enumerating anxieties.
rubric.hook_line: Don't carry your worries to bed
rubric.title: How to Actually Cast Your Cares
